basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 14.' and it opens 'Vers. 14. Ecce ejicis me hodie a facie terrae. Id est: In conspectu tuo me indignum'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 14. Ecce ejicis me hodie a facie terrae. Id est: In conspectu tuo me indignum judicas. Et a facie tua, quia videlicet ipsam meam vitam odio habens praesentiae tuae me subtraham. Omnis igitur qui invenerit me, occidet me. Quia ex tremore corporis et furiatae mentis exagitatione quicunque me invenerit, cognoscet me dignum esse, qui occidar.
